# jumpcloud_authentication_policy (Resource)

Manages a JumpCloud authentication (conditional access) policy, which allows or denies sign-ins, and can require MFA, for the targeted users when its conditions match. Settings the provider does not manage, such as the allowed MFA factors and custom error messages, keep their values from the admin console.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let a test account sign in to the user portal without MFA, only from known addresses.
resource "jumpcloud_user_group" "synthetic_test" {
  name = "Synthetic Test"
}

resource "jumpcloud_ip_list" "synthetics" {
  name = "datadog-synthetics"
  ips  = ["203.0.113.7"]
}

resource "jumpcloud_authentication_policy" "synthetic_test" {
  name           = "Synthetic test - no MFA from Datadog"
  type           = "user_portal"
  action         = "allow"
  mfa_required   = false
  user_group_ids = [jumpcloud_user_group.synthetic_test.id]
  conditions     = jsonencode({ ipAddressIn = [jumpcloud_ip_list.synthetics.id] })
}

# Require MFA on every SSO application, except from the office.
resource "jumpcloud_ip_list" "office" {
  name = "office"
  ips  = ["198.51.100.0/24"]
}

resource "jumpcloud_authentication_policy" "apps_mfa" {
  name         = "Require MFA on applications"
  type         = "application"
  action       = "allow"
  mfa_required = true
  all_users    = true
  conditions   = jsonencode({ not = { ipAddressIn = [jumpcloud_ip_list.office.id] } })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) What happens when the policy matches: `allow` or `deny`.
- `name` (String) Policy name.
- `type` (String) What the policy protects: `user_portal`, `application`, `ldap`, or `admin_portal`. Changing it replaces the policy.

### Optional

- `all_users` (Boolean) Whether the policy applies to every user. Otherwise it applies to the members of `user_group_ids`.
- `application_ids` (Set of String) For `application` policies, IDs of the SSO applications the policy protects. Empty protects every application.
- `conditions` (String) When the policy applies, as JSON in JumpCloud's condition language, built with `jsonencode`. Conditions include `ipAddressIn` (a list of `jumpcloud_ip_list` IDs), `locationIn` (`{ countries = ["US"] }`), `deviceManaged`, and `deviceEncrypted`, combined with `all`, `any`, and `not`, for example `jsonencode({ not = { ipAddressIn = [jumpcloud_ip_list.office.id] } })`. Omit to apply always.
- `description` (String) Policy description.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy is off.
- `excluded_application_ids` (Set of String) For `application` policies that protect every application, IDs of applications to leave out.
- `excluded_user_group_ids` (Set of String) IDs of user groups whose members the policy never applies to.
- `mfa_required` (Boolean) Whether an `allow` policy requires MFA. Must be `false` for `deny` policies.
- `monitor_only` (Boolean) Whether JumpCloud only logs what the policy would do instead of enforcing it.
- `user_group_ids` (Set of String) IDs of user groups whose members the policy applies to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Policy ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by ID.
terraform import jumpcloud_authentication_policy.apps_mfa 5f0c1b2a3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d
```
